LOL, I was sold on this concept that science was all about the content, ideas, and the truth when I ventured into it as a starry-eyed student. I had learned my lesson since. But it would be nice to see the scientific community return to those ideals in the last few days we have left as still a human-driven endeavor. Journals should judge papers by the results they contain, not by whether AI was used.

All of that aside, the fact that an AI can make a dynamically lit explorable 3D scene set in a realistic space elevator with realistic physics where every single object was coded by "hand" remains crazy. If you have a decent computer, it is worth trying the web version: https://upwell-tetherline.netlify.app/unity/ Or download the full Windows install from itch. io: https://emollick.itch.io/upwell I’ve been using GPT-6.2 Astra prior to launch & I found it very uneven & weird. On one hand, it was harder to steer & work with than other models. On the other, when given an ambitious project (make a space elevator ride from scratch with Blender & Unity) it could deliver well

I know a lot of people are discovering this about GPT-6.2, but the GPT models have always been obsessed with bells and drowned clock towers. Always. Forget goblins, things that GPT-5.5 really likes in its fiction: lighthouses, the ocean, maps, bells, clock towers with bells that ring impossible times, Mira Vale, resonances and echoes (Claude and Gemini love them too), secret third things (not night/day, not high/low)...
They all have the aesthetics of Ken Levine.
